title: PteronautOS
essence_lead: PteronautOS is built on ExpressLRS, transformed into a flight controller for ornithopters.
essence_body: Not a quad — no motors, no ESCs, no Betaflight. Movement is generated by waveforms driving two wing servos and a crest rudder servo.
essence_highlight: CRSF (radio) → rx_main → Ornithopter → waveform → PWM servos
arch_zephyrus_desc: MPU6050 gyroscope + Mahony AHRS + dual PID
zeph_lead: Cephalic crest rudder stabilization via MPU6050. Mahony AHRS for attitude estimation, dual PID for roll angle and yaw rate correction.
doc_lead: The manual, the gyro notes, and the web UI reference.
doc_c_ferocity_d: Stroke/return asymmetry and dwell — 0 is a pure sine.
doc_c_waveform_d: The wingbeat curve; amplitude comes from deg/s ÷ 2·freq.
doc_c_glide_d: Wing centre offset for gliding flight.
doc_c_flap_d: Centre bias during the flap stroke (−15…+15 deg).
doc_c_rudder_d: Yaw/roll blend that drives the crest rudder.
doc_c_throttle_d: How much throttle couples into ferocity.
doc_c_failsafe_d: Wings return to neutral if the link drops.
doc_wave_p1: Ferocity controls both the character and the timing of a half-stroke. Internally, the WebUI’s 0–100 setting maps to 0–8. Higher downstroke ferocity shortens the downstroke’s share of the cycle; higher return ferocity shortens the return share. The remaining time is transferred to the opposite half—there is no pause at zero.
doc_wave_p2: The per-profile Ferocity Shape control selects the high-ferocity character. At 0% it favours a finite plateau/square shape. At 100% it favours a rounded pyramidal path. Each half still uses its own ferocity, so a low-ferocity half remains elongated and sinusoidal while a high-ferocity half approaches a direct diagonal traversal.
doc_chart_halves: Each half stretched to equal width
doc_chart_aria_cycle: Wing position over the complete beat cycle
doc_read_p: A 7 / 1 combination clearly produces a short pointed downstroke and a long sinusoidal return. Exact and near-maximum values require care: the current duration law uses the amount remaining below ferocity 8. Consequently, 8 / 0 allocates only about 0.125% of the cycle to the downstroke, while even 8 / 6 allocates about 0.5%. Position remains continuous, but the requested speed and acceleration can become physically unreachable.
doc_caution_body: The explorer describes the commanded mathematical waveform, not guaranteed servo motion. Avoid extreme asymmetric settings until amplitude, frequency, linkage geometry, and servo-speed limits have been verified without aerodynamic load.
doc_lock_sync: Sync: Both sliders move together (click to cycle)

tut_lead: Practical guides for preparing the hardware, installing the hermetic firmware, and bringing a new PteronautOS airframe to life.
tut_p1: PteronautOS is not a conventional multirotor stack. It translates CRSF control into a coordinated wingbeat for two wing servos and a crest rudder, with Zephyrus stabilization remaining optional and gracefully degradable.
tut_p2: Start with the flashing guide below. Later guides will cover receiver wiring, binding, the first controlled flap, and tuning the waveform through the WebUI. Every procedure keeps the project’s core rules in view: deterministic timing, centred failsafe behaviour, and no blocking work in the flight loop.
tut_card_desc: Build the ESP8285 target, connect the receiver safely, and install the firmware.
flash_lead: Build and install the hermetic firmware using a CYCLONE ELRS 2.4GHz 7CH PWM RX Receiver as the example.
flash_p1: PteronautOS supports other receiver boards too. Sharing an ESP8285 does not make their wiring identical: the exposed GPIOs, channel assignments, programming connections, and PCB revisions can differ. The power and CH2/CH3 wiring below apply to this CYCLONE example; check your board’s pinout and supported hardware configuration before connecting another receiver.
flash_p2: Before connecting power, remove propulsive loads from the wing mechanism and make sure no servo can drive into a hard stop. Flashing is electrical work; the airframe should remain mechanically safe throughout the procedure.
flash_build_p: Clone the repository, install PlatformIO, and run the following command from the repository root. The PlatformIO project is in src; this command builds the dedicated ESP8285 receiver environment used in this example.
flash_connect_p: For this CYCLONE receiver, use the FTDI adapter’s 5 V power output for the receiver supply, not its 3.3 V power output. Its UART connections are on the signal pins of channels 2 and 3 — there is no need to locate separate UART pads.
flash_connect_note: The 5 V setting refers to receiver power. Check your adapter’s documentation: TX/RX must use ESP8285-compatible 3.3 V logic, even when the supply output is 5 V. Do not connect a second power supply at the same time.
flash_boot_p: Hold BOOT (GPIO0), unplug and reconnect the FTDI USB cable, keep BOOT held for about one second, then release it. The flashing script does not perform an automatic reset, so enter the bootloader manually before running it.
flash_write_p1: From the repository root, run the provided flashing script. It locates a working PlatformIO-bundled flashing tool and the built firmware, selects a serial port, and writes the image with the required flash settings.
flash_write_p2: Automatic port selection looks for macOS /dev/cu.* devices. If several serial devices are connected, or you are using a different operating system, explicitly select the receiver adapter’s port. Replace the example below with your actual device path.
flash_write_p3: To check bootloader communication without writing firmware, use the optional check mode. If it fails, repeat the BOOT power cycle before trying again.
flash_verify_p_a: Power-cycle the receiver without holding BOOT. Confirm that its WiFi access point and WebUI become available (SSID:
flash_verify_p_c: ), then load the configuration and verify the target name before reconnecting servos.
flash_verify_continue_rest: for pin maps and revision-specific wiring notes.
hw_lead: The boards PteronautOS runs on, and how to wire them.
hw_spec_servos_v: 3 PWM channels — left wing, right wing, crest rudder
hw_wiring_p: Three servo channels plus the MPU6050 on the I2C bus. The full pin map, I2C wiring, and v1.0/v1.1 revision differences are in the PWMP7 guide.
hw_compat_lead: Any ExpressLRS 2.4 GHz receiver based on ESP8285 + SX1280/SX1281 with PWM outputs — or a CRSF receiver paired with a CRSF→PWM converter — can run PteronautOS. Prices are approximate and vary by region.
hw_weight_note: Stock weight; removing heatshrink, connectors or housing can cut 30–60%.
hw_esp32_note: ESP32-based receivers (ESP32-C3/S3) use a different architecture and are not yet supported.
